**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Commerce 2 (0520), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2023. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer FOUR questions. All questions carry equal marks.

Instructions: 1. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. 2. The use of SIMPLE electronic calculator is allowed. 3. Show clear working in your answer booklet where necessary.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : la page de garde impose « Answer FOUR questions. All questions carry equal marks ». Le sujet imprime 6 questions, sans sections : `groupes` = ["PAPER 2"] et `regles_choix` = parmi 4 sur 6, identiques dans les 6 fichiers.

Sujet scanné (2 pages : page de garde, puis les six questions sur une seule page) ; filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ignorés. Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées. Les chiffres des exemples (FCFA) sont hypothétiques ; aucune statistique réelle, loi, taux ou institution n'est avancé au-delà des notions du programme.

Points : le sujet n'imprime que les points de chaque sous-question, jamais le total ; `points` de l'exercice est laissé vide. Pour chaque question les points imprimés totalisent 20 (Q1 : 8+6+6 ; Q2 : 6+6+8 ; Q3 : 6+8+6 ; Q4 : 8+8+4 ; Q5 : 6+8+6 ; Q6 : 8+8+4), conformément à « All questions carry equal marks » : aucun écart.

Question 2(b) : l'énoncé « Outline any TWO functions of the following departments » est ambigu (deux fonctions au total ou deux par département). Avec 6 points pour trois départements, le corrigé donne deux fonctions par département (6 fonctions, 1 point chacune) ; le candidat qui en donne deux au total n'est pas pénalisé par ce choix de rédaction.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following terms;

(i) Enterprise,

(ii) Entrepreneur,

(iii) Entrepreneurship.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Enterprise.** An enterprise is a business unit or organisation set up to produce goods or provide services in order to earn a profit. It brings together the factors of production (land, labour, capital) under the control of an owner or manager. Example: a bakery, a small transport company.

(ii) **Entrepreneur.** An entrepreneur is the person who **identifies a business opportunity, organises the factors of production, takes the risk** of starting and running the enterprise and receives the profit or bears the loss. Example: a person who opens a poultry farm after seeing that the town needs eggs.

(iii) **Entrepreneurship.** Entrepreneurship is the **process or skill** of identifying opportunities, creating a new business or improving an existing one by combining ideas, resources and risk-taking, so as to create value (goods, services, jobs and income). It includes qualities such as creativity, initiative and the willingness to take risks.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Outline any TWO functions of the following departments of an enterprise;

(i) Production,

(ii) Marketing,

(iii) Stores.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Production department** (any two)

- It **plans and carries out the making of goods** (or the provision of services) in the quantity and quality required.
- It **controls the quality and the cost** of production and looks for ways to reduce waste.

**(ii) Marketing department** (any two)

- It carries out **market research** to find out what customers want, at what price and where.
- It **promotes and sells** the products through advertising, sales promotion and distribution to customers.

**(iii) Stores department** (any two)

- It **receives, checks and stores** raw materials, tools and finished goods safely.
- It **issues materials to other departments** when requested and keeps stock records so that stock does not run out or become excessive.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain any FOUR importance of warehousing to commerce and industry.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Warehousing is the storage of goods in a suitable building from the time they are produced or bought until they are needed by buyers. It is important to commerce and industry for the following reasons.

1. **It bridges the gap between production and consumption.** Goods such as maize or cocoa are produced in a particular season but consumed all year round; the warehouse keeps them until consumers need them.
2. **It ensures a regular supply of goods.** Traders hold stock, so customers find the goods they want at any time, and factories receive raw materials without interruption.
3. **It protects goods from damage, theft and deterioration.** Good buildings, fire protection, security and, for some goods, cold rooms preserve the quality of goods.
4. **It makes buying in bulk and saving money possible.** Traders can buy large quantities at lower prices (trade discounts) and store them until they are sold.
5. **It helps to stabilise prices.** Goods are released when they are scarce and held back when they are plentiful, which avoids very big price changes.
6. **It supports the grading, packing and breaking of bulk.** Bulk goods can be sorted, packed and divided into smaller lots for retailers.
7. **Bonded warehouses allow goods to wait for customs duty.** Imported goods can be kept without paying duty until they are released for sale, which helps the importer's cash flow.
8. **It provides security for credit.** Warehouse receipts show the goods held, and the owner can use them to obtain a loan.

(Any four points, each explained, earn full marks.)

**Conclusion.** Warehousing makes trade smooth and continuous, so it benefits producers, traders and consumers.
